commits.message:
chore(deps)!: move every dependency to its latest release (0.10.0)

Peer floors rise to mobx ^7.0.3 and @promptctl/go-template-js ^0.9.0.

- mobx 7 drops observable.ref/.shallow for named observableRef and
  observableShallow, and makeObservable now requires annotations; every
  class uses TC39 accessor decorators, which register themselves, so the
  three makeObservable(this) calls are gone.
- TypeScript 7 ships no JavaScript compiler API, which the seam and
  coverage gates are built on, so typescript stays on 6.0.3, the newest
  release that has one. Its empty default for `types` is restored to
  ["node"] in tsconfig.json.
- Vite 8 compiles TypeScript with oxc, which passes TC39 decorators
  through to Node verbatim. vitest now compiles project .ts files with
  tsc and tsconfig.json, the compiler that builds dist/.

fix(release): refuse to publish a version no tag names (rich-workflows-0pr.4) (#127)

* fix(release): refuse to publish a version no tag names (rich-workflows-0pr.4)

Eleven versions of this package are on npm; five have a git tag. The ticket
assumed the other six were a backfill waiting to happen. They are not, and
finding that out is what turned this into a gate.

npm records a `gitHead` with every publish. For five of the six untagged
versions that commit no longer exists in this repository — they were branch
tips, squash-merged and deleted — and for 0.7.0 it survives only as an orphan
off master. Three of the versions (0.1.0, 0.5.0, 0.5.1) never appear in
master's history at all: master steps 0.0.1 to 0.2.0 and 0.4.0 to 0.5.2. There
is nothing left to point a tag at, so nothing about the six is recoverable.
Brandon's call was to backfill none of them and close the hole instead.

The hole is not in this workflow. `publish.yml` triggers on `v*`, so a CI
release carries a tag by construction — the tag is the trigger. Every untagged
version arrived by the other road, a hand-run `npm publish`, which no workflow
can observe: 0.8.0 appeared on the registry 26 seconds after CI failed on that
same version, and neither it nor 0.7.0 carries a provenance attestation, which
only the OIDC path can attach.

So the check moves to where both roads meet. `scripts/verify-release-tag.mjs`
runs on `prepublishOnly` — which npm fires for every `npm publish` and for
nothing else, before the tarball is built, aborting on a non-zero exit — and
refuses any tree whose HEAD carries no tag naming the version about to ship. It
fails closed: a tree where git cannot answer is refused rather than assumed,
so `rm -rf .git` is not a bypass. It is plain ESM on bare node because the
publish job deliberately has no node_modules; `tsconfig.scripts.json` now
type-checks it, so lint still covers it.

publish.yml's own "Verify tag matches package.json version" step is deleted in
the same change rather than left as a second rule about one invariant. The one
case where it was stricter, and why that case costs nothing, is written where
it was removed. The mismatched-tag interlock is unchanged: a tag disagreeing
with package.json still cannot reach the registry, so it remains a safe way to
exercise the release path end to end.

Verified: `npm publish --dry-run` on untagged master is refused by the guard
and aborted by npm; the same tree with the matching tag present publishes. The
npm lifecycle behaviour the guard depends on was established against a
throwaway package rather than assumed — `prepublishOnly` fires on publish and
dry-run, not on `npm pack` or `npm install`.

lint clean, 2478 tests pass, actionlint clean.

* fix(release): ask origin for the tag, not the local ref store

The guard read `git tag --points-at HEAD`, which a tag that was never pushed
satisfies. That is not a lesser version of the failure this gate exists to
prevent — it is the same one: the six untagged releases are missing tags on
origin, and a tag living only on a laptop leaves npm holding a version origin
cannot describe. Review caught it.

So the question changes rather than gaining a second half: `git ls-remote --tags
origin refs/tags/vX refs/tags/vX^{}` compared against `git rev-parse HEAD`. One
question, one authority. The peeled pattern is load-bearing — for an annotated
tag `ls-remote` reports the tag object's own sha under the plain ref, so
querying only that ref would refuse every annotated release. Checked before
relying on it: `ls-remote` against this repository succeeds with no credentials
at all, so the publish job does not depend on `persist-credentials`.

This also makes the answer independent of workflow config, which fixes a claim
that was wrong. A comment in publish.yml argued the guard would permit a commit
carrying two version tags; the checkout there runs with `--no-tags` and a single
refspec, so the co-located tag is not on disk and the guard would have refused.
Reading origin removes the dependency rather than restating it.

Two more from the same review:

The refusal quoted `error.message.split("\n")[0]`, which execFileSync fills with
"Command failed: <argv>" for every non-zero exit — the same uninformative string
whatever went wrong, while the cause sits in stderr one line below. It now
quotes stderr, so "fatal: not a git repository" reaches the reader, and a test
pins that rather than the generic substring.

`PackageManifest`'s doc comment said it models only the published surface, which
`scripts` is not. The comment now states the principle the interface actually
follows and keeps the devDependencies warning at full strength.

The remedy line is now read off the same data as the refusal: offering `git tag
vX` when origin already carries that name handed the reader a command that would
fail on the tag it had just printed.

Tests rebuilt around a real bare origin on disk — no network — including the
never-pushed case and a tag pointing at a different commit.

lint clean, 2480 tests pass, actionlint clean.

* fix(release): state the guard's guarantee narrowly and pin the shared-commit case

The deleted GITHUB_REF_NAME step was not strictly weaker than the guard:
a commit carrying both the manifest's tag and another version tag
publishes the manifest's version without complaint. Say that in
publish.yml and pin it in the suite beside the ordinary forgotten bump,
which is still refused.
